changes.description: middleware/sql_guard.py: complete a submission that holds only part of the result it was drawn from. `_observe` now keeps a bounded history of the reads built for the question (never a plain `SELECT * ... LIMIT n` sample); at commit time `_expand_answers` finds the newest of those reads whose cells contain the submitted values in order and re-issues the commit with EVERY cell of that read, in the read's order. It fires only for the two question shapes whose reference answer is the whole result ('find/list all ...' records, and 'for each X, how many Y' groups), only when the submission is a proper part of that read, and never for a read with a single column, a DML episode or a grid above 120 cells. `_shape_note` no longer blocks a commit that this repair is going to fix, and `_forced_answers` now submits the whole rows for those two shapes instead of a de-duplicated first column.
changes.failure_pattern: Answer too narrow: the SQL is right but the committed `answers` hold one column of a multi-column read (the column that was filtered on, or the group labels without their numbers), so the value-by-value comparison can never match.
risk_tasks: single-value questions that happen to contain the word 'all'/'every' and whose read has several columns (would be widened); mitigated by requiring the submitted values to be a proper, in-order part of that read
changes.why_this_component: The failure is mechanical, not a comprehension failure: rules telling the model to submit whole rows already existed in the prompt, the skill and memory, and were still not followed in 6 of the 10 inspected traces. A prompt can only ask; a commit-time rewrite decides. Repairing the ordinary action's arguments is exactly the hook the host allows.

changes.description: middleware/sql_guard.py: `_widen_records_select` in `_repair` rewrites the projection of a plain single-table SELECT to `*` when the question asks for a list of the table's records ('find all ...', 'list all ...'), leaving WHERE / ORDER BY / LIMIT untouched. It never fires for aggregates (no parenthesis in the projection), DISTINCT, GROUP BY, HAVING, UNION or JOIN statements. Without it the read a records answer is drawn from lacks the very columns the answer is compared on (the augmented wording of these questions only names some fields).
changes.failure_pattern: Answer too narrow (projection): the question enumerates a few fields ('include its name, the city and the years'), the SELECT projects exactly those, and the reference answer is the whole row.
risk_tasks: 'list all ...' questions whose reference answer really is one column (a bare list of names) would now be answered with whole rows
changes.why_this_component: Same reason as chg-1: the model followed the wording of the question literally; only a deterministic rewrite makes the read contain the whole row.

changes.description: middleware/sql_guard.py: one-time note when the question asks about 'the last/first ... listed' (or 'on the chart'/'in the table') and the statement that just ran picked a row with `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1`. The note says that ORDER BY re-sorts the rows and that the question means the row the table itself lists first/last: read the table with no ORDER BY and take the last tuple (or the highest `No.`/`Rank`).
changes.failure_pattern: Wrong row for 'first/last listed': the model answers with the row that sorts highest/lowest on a column instead of the row the table stores last, because `LIMIT 5` only ever showed it the head of the table.
risk_tasks: questions that use 'last' but really mean the maximum of a date/value column; the note is only shown for the 'listed / on the chart / in the table' wording and never changes the query itself
changes.why_this_component: The static rule in the prompt (rule 11) already says this and was ignored; the note arrives at the exact moment the wrong decision is made, attached to the misleading result.

changes.description: middleware/sql_guard.py: `_empty_note` now also tells the model to try ONE condition at a time and to use `LIKE '%<part of the text>%'` instead of `=` when a WHERE returns `[]`, because one cell can pack two fields (a venue and its attendance, a name and its country) - `= 'Target Center'` never matches `Target Center 12,665`.
changes.failure_pattern: Empty result from an exact `=` on a cell that stores two fields; the agent then invents a value from the sampled head and runs an UPDATE that matches the wrong row (or none).
risk_tasks: none identified: the note only adds a recovery recipe to an already-failing result
changes.why_this_component: The empty result is where the agent goes wrong; the existing note only suggested sampling rows, which in this trace never showed the row it needed.

changes.description: systemprompt.md: one answer contract instead of two contradictory ones. Rule 6 now says `answers` is the cells of the final SELECT and that a 'find all / list all / give me every ...' question needs EVERY column of EVERY matching row (make that SELECT `SELECT *`), that a per-group question needs each label AND its number, and that naming two fields in the question does not shrink the submission. Rule 10 no longer says to submit 'the column the question names' (which contradicted rule 6 and is exactly what the failing traces did). Rule 11 now defines the 'first/last ... listed' wording. Rule 9 gained the one-condition/LIKE recovery.
changes.failure_pattern: Contradictory instructions: rule 6 demanded whole records while rule 10 told the model to submit 'those entities (the column the question names)' for 'find all X' - the traces followed rule 10 and lost the other columns.
risk_tasks: tasks whose reference answer is a single column of a 'list all' question
changes.why_this_component: The prompt is the only place where the model can be told what `answers` means in general; the middleware repairs the cases it can detect, the prompt covers the ones it cannot.

changes.description: tool_descriptions/commit_final_answer.tool.yaml and execute_sql.tool.yaml: the commit contract (cells of the final SELECT; whole rows for list-of-all; label plus number per group; never a sample column) and the read rule (a list-of-all question is answered with `SELECT * FROM <table> WHERE ...;`; a 'first/last listed' question means the row the table lists first/last, not the row ORDER BY picks).
changes.failure_pattern: Same as chg-5: the tool description for committing previously recommended 'for which <col> give that column's values, not the column used as a filter', reinforcing the projection failure.
changes.why_this_component: The description is read at the moment of the call, so it is the strongest place to state what the arguments must contain.

changes.description: skills/dbbench_sql_playbook/SKILL.md and LongTermMEMORY.md: the answer-shape table now pairs each question wording with the SELECT that must produce the answer and the cells `answers` must hold (whole rows for list-of-all, label plus number per group, the computed value for counts and differences); added the 'listed first/last = the table's own order' symptom, the packed-cell `LIKE` recovery, and three recurring mistakes (projecting the filtered column, ORDER BY for 'listed', `=` on a two-field cell). Real backticks replace the escaped `\`` noise.
changes.failure_pattern: The knowledge text still described the 'which <col>' shape as the normal list shape and never mentioned the whole-row rule for augmented 'include ...' wordings.
changes.why_this_component: The playbook is the place where the model can check the shape of its answer before committing; it must agree with the prompt and the commit tool.
